author: Russell Contreras
title: Beyoncé boosts TSU's Ocean of Soul - NewsBreak
text:
By Russell Contreras ,
17 hours ago
Beyoncé's BeyGOOD Foundation has awarded Texas Southern University's Ocean of Soul Marching Band $100,000 after more than 200 of its musicians joined her nationally televised "Beyoncé Bowl" performance.
Why it matters: The hometown investment turns a star-studded performance into scholarships and long-term support for students at one of Houston's most prominent historically Black universities.
State of play: TSU said the money will fund scholarships for band members, recruiting and retention efforts, and upgrades to infrastructure and technology.
Zoom in: The Ocean of Soul performed with Beyoncé during the Houston Texans-Baltimore Ravens Christmas Day halftime show in 2024, streamed on Netflix.
Zoom out: Beyoncé has repeatedly used major performances to elevate HBCUs, including launching Homecoming scholarships after her landmark 2018 Coachella set.
What they're saying: TSU President J.W. Crawford III called the gift a commitment to "empowering our student musicians" and their artistic expression.
Context: The Houston native launched BeyGOOD in 2013.
Its work has expanded from disaster relief and housing to scholarships, small-business grants and investments in underserved communities. The bottom line: Beyoncé is converting Houston pride into tangible opportunities for the next generation of HBCU performers.
